readings.title: The Rebellion of the Congregation
readings.text: [Numbers 14:1] And all the congregation lifted up their voice and cried, and the people wept that night. [2] And all the children of Yisra’ĕl grumbled against Mosheh and against Aharon, and all the congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Mitsrayim! Or if only we had died in this wilderness! [3] “And why is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> bringing us to this land to fall by the sword, that our wives and children should become a prey? Would it not be better for us to turn back to Mitsrayim?” [4] And they said to each other, “Let us appoint a leader and turn back to Mitsrayim.” [5] Then Mosheh and Aharon fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl. [6] And Yehoshua son of Nun, and Kalĕḇ son of Yephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their garments, [7] and they spoke to all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “The land we passed through to spy out is an exceedingly good land. [8] “If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has delighted in us, then <dn>He</dn> shall bring us into this land and give it to us, ‘a land which flows with milk and honey.’ [9] “Only, do not rebel against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor fear the people of the land, for they are our bread. Their defence has turned away from them, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with us. Do not fear them.” [10] And all the congregation said to stone them with stones. Then the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared in the Tent of Appointment before all the children of Yisra’ĕl. [11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“How long shall this people scorn <dn>Me</dn>? And how long shall they not trust <dn>Me</dn>, with all the signs which <dn>I</dn> have done in their midst?</dq> [12] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> strike them with the pestilence and dispossess them, and make of you a nation greater and mightier than they.”</dq>

readings.title: The Intercession of Mosheh
readings.text: [Numbers 14:13] And Mosheh said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Then the Mitsrites shall hear it, for by <dn>Your</dn> power <dn>You</dn> brought these people up from their midst, [14] and they shall say to the inhabitants of this land that they have heard that <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, are in the midst of these people, that <dn>You</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, are seen eye to eye and that <dn>Your</dn> cloud stands over them, and <dn>You</dn> go before them in a column of cloud by day and in a column of fire by night. [15] “Now if <dn>You</dn> shall kill these people as one man, then the nations who have heard of <dn>Your</dn> report shall speak, saying, [16] ‘Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was not able to bring this people to the land which <dn>He</dn> swore to them, therefore <dn>He</dn> slew them in the wilderness.’ [17] “And now, please, let the power of my <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be great, as <dn>You</dn> have spoken, saying, [18] ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is patient and of great kindness, forgiving crookedness and transgression, but by no means leaving unpunished; visiting the crookedness of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation.’ [19] “Forgive, please, the crookedness of this people, according to the greatness of <dn>Your</dn> kindness, as <dn>You</dn> have forgiven this people, from Mitsrayim even until now.” [20] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have forgiven, according to your word;</dq> [21] <dq>but truly, as <dn>I</dn> live, all the earth shall be filled with the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>;</dq> [22] <dq>for all these men who have seen <dn>My</dn> esteem and <dn>My</dn> signs which <dn>I</dn> did in Mitsrayim and in the wilderness, and have tried <dn>Me</dn> now these ten times, and have not obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice,</dq> [23] <dq>they shall certainly not see the land of which <dn>I</dn> swore to their fathers, nor any of those who scorned <dn>Me</dn> see it.</dq> [24] <dq>“But <dn>My</dn> servant Kalĕḇ, because he has a different spirit in him and has followed <dn>Me</dn> completely, <dn>I</dn> shall bring him into the land where he went, and his seed shall inherit it.</dq> [25] <dq>“Since the Amalĕqites and the Kena’anites are dwelling in the valley, turn tomorrow and set out into the wilderness by the Way of the Sea of Reeds.”</dq>

readings.title: Sentence and Failed Invasion
readings.text: [Numbers 14:26] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying, [27] <dq>“How long shall <dn>I</dn> bear with this evil congregation who grumble against <dn>Me</dn>? <dn>I</dn> have heard the grumblings which the children of Yisra’ĕl make against <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>“Say to them, ‘As <dn>I</dn> live,’ says <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘as you have spoken in <dn>My</dn> ears, so <dn>I</dn> do to you:</dq> [29] <dq>‘The carcases of you who have grumbled against <dn>Me</dn> are going to fall in this wilderness, all of you who were registered, according to your entire number, from twenty years old and above.</dq> [30] <dq>‘None of you shall come into the land except Kalĕḇ son of Yephunneh and Yehoshua son of Nun, which <dn>I</dn> swore <dn>I</dn> would make you dwell in.</dq> [31] <dq>‘But your little ones, whom you said would become a prey, <dn>I</dn> shall bring in, and they shall know the land which you have rejected.</dq> [32] <dq>‘But as for you, your carcases are going to fall in this wilderness.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And your sons shall be wanderers in the wilderness forty years, and shall bear your whoredoms, until your carcases are consumed in the wilderness.</dq> [34] <dq>‘According to the number of the days in which you spied out the land, forty days – a day for a year, a day for a year – you are to bear your crookednesses forty years, and you shall know <dn>My</dn> breaking off.’</dq> [35] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> have spoken: <dn>I</dn> shall certainly do this to all this evil congregation who are gathered together against <dn>Me</dn>. In this wilderness they are consumed, and there they die.”</dq> [36] And the men whom Mosheh sent to spy out the land, who returned and made all the congregation grumble against him by bringing an evil report of the land, [37] even those men who brought the evil report of the land, died by the plague before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [38] But Yehoshua son of Nun and Kalĕḇ son of Yephunneh remained alive, of the men who went to spy out the land. [39] And Mosheh spoke these words to all the children of Yisra’ĕl, and the people mourned greatly. [40] And they rose up early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “See, we are here, and we shall go up to the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has promised, for we have sinned.” [41] But Mosheh said, “Why do you now transgress the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? For it does not prosper. [42] “Do not go up, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not in your midst, lest you be smitten before your enemies. [43] “For the Amalĕqites and the Kena’anites are there before you, and you shall fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not with you.” [44] But they presumed to go up to the top of the mountain, but the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and Mosheh did not leave the camp. [45] And the Amalĕqites and the Kena’anites who dwelt in that mountain came down and struck them, and beat them down, as far as Ḥormah.

readings.title: Offerings in the Promised Land
readings.text: [Numbers 15:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land of your dwellings, which <dn>I</dn> am giving to you,</dq> [3] <dq>and you make an offering by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow or as a voluntary offering or in your appointed times, to make a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, from the herd or from the flock,</dq> [4] <dq>then he who brings his offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall bring a grain offering of one-tenth of an ĕphah of fine flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of oil,</dq> [5] <dq>and one-fourth of a hin of wine as a drink offering you prepare with the burnt offering or the sacrifice, for each lamb.</dq> [6] <dq>‘Or for a ram you prepare as a grain offering two-tenths of an ĕphah of fine flour mixed with one-third of a hin of oil,</dq> [7] <dq>and as a drink offering you bring one-third of a hin of wine as a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And when you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering, or as a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow, or as a peace offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [9] <dq>then he shall bring with the young bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ĕphah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil,</dq> [10] <dq>and bring as a drink offering half a hin of wine as an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [11] <dq>‘This is what is done for each bull, or for each ram, or for each female lamb or young goat.</dq> [12] <dq>‘According to the number that you prepare, so you do for each one according to their number.</dq> [13] <dq>‘All who are native-born do these matters in this way, in bringing an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And when a stranger sojourns with you, or whoever is among you throughout your generations, and would make an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as you do, so he does.</dq> [15] <dq>‘One law is for you of the assembly and for the stranger who sojourns with you, a law forever throughout your generations. As you are, so is the stranger before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [16] <dq>‘One torah and one right-ruling is for you and for the stranger who sojourns with you.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Sins of Ignorance and Presumption
readings.text: [Numbers 15:17] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [18] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land to which <dn>I</dn> bring you,</dq> [19] <dq>then it shall be, when you eat of the bread of the land, that you present a contribution to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [20] <dq>‘Present a cake of the first of your dough as a contribution, as a contribution of the threshing-floor, so you present it.</dq> [21] <dq>‘Of the first of your dough you are to give to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> a contribution throughout your generations.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And when you sin by mistake, and do not observe all these commands which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken to Mosheh,</dq> [23] <dq>all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded you by the hand of Mosheh, from the day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> began commanding and onward throughout your generations,</dq> [24] <dq>then it shall be, if it is done by mistake, without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall prepare one young bull as a burnt offering, as a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with its grain offering and its drink offering, according to the right-ruling, and one male goat as a sin offering.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And the priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and it shall be forgiven them, for it was by mistake. And they shall bring their offering, an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and their sin offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for their mistake.</dq> [26] <dq>‘And it shall be forgiven all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl and the stranger who sojourns in their midst, because all the people were in the mistake.</dq> [27] <dq>‘And if any being sins by mistake, then he shall bring a female goat a year old as a sin offering.</dq> [28] <dq>‘And the priest shall make atonement for the being who strays by mistake, when he sins by mistake before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to make atonement for him, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq> [29] <dq>‘For him who is native-born among the children of Yisra’ĕl and for the stranger who sojourns in their midst, there is one torah for him who does it by mistake.</dq> [30] <dq>‘But the being who does it with a high hand, whether he is native-born or a stranger, that one reviles <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and that being shall be cut off from among his people.</dq> [31] <dq>‘Because he has despised the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and has broken <dn>His</dn> command, that being shall certainly be cut off, his crookedness is upon him.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Violation of the Sabbath
readings.text: [Numbers 15:32] And while the children of Yisra’ĕl were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day. [33] And those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Mosheh and to Aharon, and to all the congregation. [34] And they put him in under guard, because it had not been declared what should be done to him. [35] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“The man shall certainly be put to death, all the congregation stoning him with stones outside the camp.”</dq> [36] And all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Mosheh.

readings.title: The Law of Tassels
readings.text: [Numbers 15:37] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [38] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them to make tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a blue cord in the tassel of the corners.</dq> [39] <dq>“And it shall be to you for a tassel, and you shall see it, and shall remember all the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and shall do them, and not search after your own heart and your own eyes, which you went whoring after,</dq> [40] <dq>so that you remember, and shall do all <dn>My</dn> commands, and be set-apart to <dn>your Elohim</dn>.</dq> [41] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH your Elohim</dn>, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to be <dn>your Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH your Elohim</dn>.”</dq>
